messages:
ops-bot: Incident alert — p99 latency spike on /v1/generate in prod (us-west) starting ~2035006765. SLO breaches: p95=220ms->400ms, p99=1.8s->5.2s. Streaming stalls observed. Auto-incident created: INC-2035. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/streams?orgId=1
maria: oncall here, looking...
sam: saw a sharp bump in batching queue length at 2035006762, correlates with mixed seqlen traffic. logs snippet: ```batcher.enqueue=1240 batcher.dequeue=1180 avg_wait_ms=85```
lee: GPU side shows increased page faults around the same time, KV cache churn looks high (>40% evictions)
maria: possible hypothesis: large mixed-seq requests are filling batches and causing long waits for streaming lanes -> tail and stalls. quick mitigations: reduce max batch cap, enable seqlen preemption, isolate noisy customers
devin: quick config change ready. propose: `max_batch_bytes` 16777216 -> 8388608 and `seqlen_preempt_ms` 50 -> 20
maria: applying to pool-A now: `curl -s -XPOST https://infra-api.prod/pools/pool-A/config -d '{"max_batch_bytes":8388608,"seqlen_preempt_ms":20}'`
ops-bot: config rollout started by maria at 2035006890 (change-id: cfg-2035-1)
sam: watching traces — p99 down from 5.2s -> ~2.4s within 90s of rollout, good signal
lee: still seeing streaming stalls for some very long requests (>12k tokens), those still cause paging and kv-thrashing
maria: second mitigation: enable aggressive KV eviction for long-prefix entries (temp): ```evict_policy: {"type":"LRU","min_age_ms":200}```
devin: I'm going to route the top-3 noisy customers to dedicated nodes to reduce interference: `route set --customer beta-corp --pool dedicated-b`
infra-bot: Route change applied (route-id r-2035-beta)
maria: tagging all impacted traces with `x-incident:INC-2035` for later analysis. also started a sampling job to capture full request/response for affected flows
sam: added an additional short-term tweak: reduce batching window for streaming lanes from 10ms -> 6ms (`batch_window_ms=6`) to prioritize low-latency token flushing
lee: still seeing a handful of p99 outliers — digging into scheduler fairness: big requests sometimes preempt the slot and prevent KV reuse for small streaming slots
maria: immediate plan: 1) keep reduced max_batch cap, 2) enforce seqlen-aware slot assignment (small streaming lanes get reserved slots), 3) scale pool-A by +2 nodes, 4) keep KV-evict for hot prefixes, 5) continue trace capture
devin: scaling +2 nodes initiated (scale-op: scale-2035-1)
maria: handoff to @lee for the next shift at 2035007000 UTC — monitor p99; if >1.5s, page infra lead and escalate. notes left in incident channel
lee: ack. leaving runbook notes:
- logs: s3://prod-logs/batcher/pool-A/2035/
- temp configs: cfg-2035-1 (max_batch_bytes=8MB), cfg-2035-2 (seqlen_preempt=20ms), batch_window_stream=6ms
- sample traces: /traces/incidents/INC-2035
- customers impacted (observed): beta-corp (elevated latency, no errors), gamma-samples (increased latency + intermittent stalled streaming)
maria: postmortem summary (prelim): root cause = continuous batching scheduler + mixed sequence-length workload causing unfair scheduling and KV cache churn; exacerbated by paging under load. Immediate mitigations: batch cap, seqlen preemption, KV-evict, route isolation, scale up. Next steps: scheduler fairness fix, better seqlen bucketing, unit tests for mixed-seqlen p99, long-term KV eviction tuning
ops-bot: Incident INC-2035 status updated -> mitigated; severity: high -> monitoring (2035007055)
lee: continuing to watch dashboards and traces for next 30m. will reopen if regression observed. ping @maria @devin if anything pops up.
